cards.explanation: The answer is the whole army. Joshua, Israel's leader, gets a full-roster order this time: “Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai.” Last time it was only about three thousand men (Joshua 7:4). That's the difference between moving a couch with one friend and moving it with the whole group chat. Everybody shows up.

The answer is True. The LORD says to do to Ai and its king as was done to Jericho and its king, "…except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves." That's a change from Jericho. I think that's a pretty big deal for the people carrying the load.

The answer is to set up an ambush behind the city. The LORD says, "Set up an ambush behind the city." Nobody has to storm the front gate and hope for the best. The plan gets Ai out of the front door while some of Israel's men wait behind it. It's patient work, like waiting for the timer instead of opening the oven every thirty seconds.

The answer is that they flee from them. Joshua says that when Ai comes out against them, "…we will flee from them." That's the plan, not a panic, friends. The running is the bait that pulls Ai away from its city.

The answer is that they'll think Israel is running like before. Joshua says the men of Ai will say, “The Israelites are running away from us as they did before.” Joshua is counting on what happened the first time to shape what they say this time. It's like when a friend has bailed on you twice, so the third time you say "he's bailing again" before you even check your phone. Joshua's plan has Israel flee so that Ai follows and gets drawn away from the city.

The answer is True. Joshua tells the men in ambush, “…you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.” That's the plan for while Israel is running away. Later the LORD tells Joshua to hold out his battle lance toward Ai, and as soon as he does, the men in ambush rise quickly (Joshua 8:18, 19). The ambush crew spends a lot of time waiting, and then they move fast.
The answer is burn. Joshua says, "…set it on fire." That's the order once the ambush has taken the city. Later the smoke rising is what Ai sees when they look back (Joshua 8:20).
The answer is False. Joshua got up early and mobilized his men, and "…he and the elders of Israel marched before them up to Ai." He goes in front, not behind. The troops follow him.

The answer is north, friends! The troops “…camped to the north of it, with the valley between them and the city.” The other group lay in ambush to the west, between Bethel and Ai (Joshua 8:12). One group is in front of the city, and the other is set up behind it. The king of Ai did not know about the ambush (Joshua 8:14).

The answer is False. The king of Ai hurries out early in the morning, but "…he did not know that an ambush had been set up against him behind the city." He sees one army and doesn't know about the other. That's why the plan works.
The answer is toward the wilderness. Joshua and all Israel "…fled toward the wilderness." They let themselves be beaten back, and Ai follows. That pulls the men of Ai away from their city.

The answer is False. The text says, “Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel, leaving the city wide open while they pursued Israel.” Every man went out after Israel. There were no men left behind to guard the city. That's exactly the opening the men in ambush take.

The answer is his battle lance. The LORD says, "Hold out your battle lance toward Ai, for into your hand I will deliver the city." Joshua holds it out, and the men in ambush rise as soon as he does. It works as the signal.

The answer is smoke. “When the men of Ai turned and looked back, the smoke of the city was rising into the sky.” The men in ambush had rushed into the city, captured it and immediately set it on fire (Joshua 8:19). So when Ai looks back, the smoke is what they see. The text goes on to say they could not escape in any direction.

The answer is False. The text says the men of Ai have no way out in any direction. Their city is burning behind them, and the troops who had fled to the wilderness turn on their pursuers. Then those in the ambush come out of the city, and the men of Ai are trapped between the Israelite forces on both sides (Joshua 8:22).

The answer is trapped between Israel on both sides. The men of Ai "…were trapped between the Israelite forces on both sides." The ambush came out of the city, and the troops who fled turned around. It's a heavy part of the story, friends, and the text says it plainly.

The answer is the king of Ai. “But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.” The men of Ai who pursued Israel were struck down until no survivor or fugitive remained (Joshua 8:22). The king is the one taken alive instead. Joshua deals with him later in the passage.

The answer is True. “Israel took for themselves only the cattle and plunder of that city, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.” At the start, the LORD told Joshua they could carry off the plunder and livestock for themselves (Joshua 8:2). So Israel takes what the LORD allowed and does it as He commanded. Nothing more is taken. And this story isn't over, friends, so keep baking.

The answer is a large pile of rocks. The text says “…over it they raised a large pile of rocks, which remains to this day.” That's after the body was taken down at sunset and thrown down at the entrance of the city gate. It's a heavy ending for a heavy passage, and the text tells it plainly. The rocks are still there when the writer tells it.
